name: nvjpeg_format_to_ycbcr
desc: nvjpeg::format_to_ycbcr_kernel<InputFormat_t4 (planar BGR), 420(2), ColorModelToYUV, LaunchParams<32,8>> from libnvjpeg sm_90. Planar BGR -> planar YCbCr with 4:2:0 chroma subsampling on output. Each thread handles a 2x2 pixel block (edge pixels clamped to w-1/h-1). Y = 0.299R+0.587G+0.114B; Cb = -0.168736R-0.331264G+0.5B+128; Cr = 0.5R-0.418688G-0.081312B+128 (verified JFIF coeffs, channel order ch0=B/ch1=G/ch2=R decoded from SASS). Cb/Cr output = average of the 4 block chroma values. Param layout from EIATTR_KPARAM_INFO: in@0x210, inSize@0x250, out@0x258, roi@0x298.
blocker: Two independent x86-lifter gaps, both confirmed by inspecting lift/lifter.py and the lifted .ll: (1) lift_i2f (lift/lifter.py:2085) ignores the .B1/.B2/.B3 BYTE-SELECT modifier on a source register operand (parser DOES preserve operand.suffix='B1', verified). 'I2F.U8 R11, R16.B1' is lifted identically to 'I2F.U8 R14, R16' -> both take byte 0. The kernel packs two horizontally-adjacent input pixels into one U16 and reads col1 via .B1, so every ODD output column collapses to the col-0 value. (2) lift_fmul (lift/lifter.py:1097) drops the .D2 result-divisor modifier: 'FMUL.D2 sum, 0.5' should be sum*0.5/2 = sum*0.25 (the 4-pixel chroma average) but lifts to plain sum*0.5, doubling the chroma deviation from 128. Independent host reference (correct JFIF math + correct .B1/.D2 semantics): even/byte-0 columns of Y all MATCH (confirms channel order, coefficients, addressing, grid all correct); only the odd/byte-1 columns and all Cb/Cr fail. mismatches = 128/192 (badY=64 [all odd cols], badCb=32, badCr=32). NOT a forced pass.
ground_truth: x86-lifted FAILS independent reference (128/192) due to lifter .B1 byte-select + .D2 divisor gaps; conversion math/channel-order/ABI all verified correct on byte-0 columns.
